wait until you see how this works. So basically you can create your own set of digital co-workers
who specialize in different things and you message them just like you would an actual
co-worker. If you've never experienced an AI teammate working on your behalf, you're going
to want to try this out. Why? What do you mean? Well, for example, here's my crew of bots. I have

marketing and it sends me reports. I have another one I named Lucy who researches a brand's recent
campaigns, finds their best performing creative across all of social, and then sends me a one

deliverable. That's why I think this could be the thing that finally brings AI agents to the masses.

#GooglePartner From never making a stained glass window... to building one from scratch! • now | just need to install it...who's ready for a part 2?

transcript.text: I've been dreaming of adding a stained glass window to my stairwell for years, but there's
just one problem.
I've never made a stained glass window before.
So before ordering a single supply, I used Chrome to help me figure out exactly what
I needed.
I had three different options for stained glass kits opened, and I just wasn't sure,
so I actually asked Gemini and Chrome to compare the pricing and shipping times across the
open tab so I can get the best deal possible.
The neighboring home to mine is bright red, and I discovered that if I use green glass,
I can actually neutralize the bounce, so we're gonna go with green shades of glass.
I started by cutting down a bunch of glass squares for the window with a little template,
and the cost of glass definitely adds up, so thankfully I was able to use Gemini in Chrome
to estimate a rough amount of glass that I would actually need to cover my entire window,
which ended up being the perfect amount.
I ensured to vary the shades of glass and also textures as I worked on this window just
to make it really organic.
With every cut, glass placement, and solder, my window panel grew, and so did my excitement
for the project because this process was just so straightforward.
I'm about 75% complete, and I cannot wait for us to install this window in my next video.
Make sure to follow along for the reveal, and go try Chrome for yourself to see what projects
you can unlock.

🚨A man has been charged after police say he ran over an Eastpointe officer with a trailer and led officers on a chase into Detroit.

Police responded to English Gardens at 22501 Kelly Road around 1:40 a.m. Friday, Sept. 25, after a report of a man prowling inside the closed business. Officers stopped a landscaping truck driven by Jeremy Johnson, 38, and said its trailer had no plate and carried items from the store.

When told to get out because he was under arrest, Johnson started the truck and accelerated, police said. The truck struck an officer at the driver’s door, and the trailer rolled over his legs. The officer was treated and released.

Police said Johnson tried to hit several police vehicles during the chase. His damaged trailer scattered landscaping tools across the road, damaging at least one police car. He eventually bailed out, fled on foot and tried to sit on a porch and disguise himself before being arrested.

At arraignment, Johnson said he wasn’t a danger to the community and had smoked marijuana, adding that he normally doesn’t buy it from people he meets at gas stations.

Magistrate Makoski of 38th District Court called Johnson a danger to the community and ordered him held on $1 million cash or surety bond.

What Root Bio is trying to solve is the hardest and most important biological problems outside human pharma.
We use AI to design completely new molecules for food production or agriculture.
Our first molecule is reducing methane emissions from cows.
We basically have done this whole discovery process manually.
But now because of AI and automation, we can do it in months.
But we are also working on antibiotic alternatives and our products always increase value for the farmer and do something good for the world.
This is what I really love.

transcript.text: It's now been four years since I started building a tunnel system under my suburban house.
This is a recap of what has become a huge project with hundreds of tons of rock excavated
and many aspects of construction and engineering.
At the beginning, pandemic-induced boredom reignited my childhood yearning for the mines
and I cut into my basement wall and made a portal to the underworld.
I quickly ran out of space to pile the rock, but fortunately have a large window well where
I was able to build a hoist and hopper to raise loads of rock.
Two hundred and fifty tons so far, all loaded into dumpsters or saved for use.
In fact, I struck several interesting layers of hardened metamorphic rock which can be used
for building and crafting.
I planned to use the larger pieces for constructing my castle.
Until now, I excavated a thirty-foot entry staircase, an antechamber, and another lower tunnel.
All required electrical, plumbing, ventilation, and concrete work.
A lot of concrete work.
Either installed as blocks, pumped in by truck, or mixed by hand.
Fifty cubic yards so far.
During the second year, increasing public exposure as well as justified local concern caused the
project to be shut down by the city for lack of permits.
Basically, they said it's excavations.
Then you're pulling stuff out of the basement.
Yeah, a little bit.
I spent the next year going back and forth developing plans, responding to questions, and submitting
documents.
And it got approved.
I reopened the mine, and since then I've been on a table.
restored the hoist hopper, completed excavation of the lower tunnel, and the
antechamber ceiling, which required a mountain of form lumber, and burned my
pocketbook. To lower costs, I got trucks of aggregate and sand and built a pipe
to deliver the material into my basement. The sandpipe got clogged, so I added a
vibrator. Now I can mix by hand. Recently, I completed three manual pours, a new sump
basin, the lower tunnel staircase, and the upper staircase. The last took 21 hours.
There is a little more work to do on the current phase of the tunnel, but I am
already working on plans for the next, which will be more extensive and require
a systematic rethink of the tools and techniques used for excavation. I have
ideas, but will need big infrastructure upgrades.

transcript.text: First up here we have a liquid level indicator.
Here we have a talking keychain clock.
This simple orange tool is called a pocket money brailler and is a great way to add braille to United States currency to make it tactile.
This small rubber tool is designed to hold a bottle of eyedrops and make it easier to get it into the eye by resting the device on the nose and squeezing in the eyedrop.
Here we have a credit card sized piece of plastic with a rectangular cutout that is designed to help with signing documents and it is called a signature guide.
Here we have an of glove which is designed to grab things out of the oven without getting burned.
Here we have another great option these are called bump dot stickers and can be added to appliances to make the buttons tactile.
Here we have aluminum braille tags that can be sewn into clothing to help someone tell the different color clothing apart.
Here we have a non-cut glove so when cutting fruits and vegetables and other food the person is safe from cutting themselves.
Here we have rubber sock holders.
They are designed to keep socks paired when going through the laundry.
They can be wrapped around a pair and go through to keep them organized.
For someone with some usable vision having these pads of high contrast black lined paper can be really helpful.
Next up here we have a high contrast cutting board black on one side white on the other.
And lastly here we have a high contrast coaster with yellow edges and ridges to keep drinks in place.
Here we have a high contrast coaster with yellow edges and a pair of gloves.
Here we have a high contrast coaster with yellow edges.

transcript.text: I get asked this question a lot.
How can I hit a million followers on Facebook?
And now that I have almost 5 million followers on Facebook, I think I've learned a thing
or two.
My first tip might sound super obvious, but share your real life.
People like real people.
I can guarantee you that the things you're going through, other people are too.
And honestly, I think social media could use a little bit more real life stuff.
Now it took me about a year to get to a million followers on Facebook.
So this is not something that just happens overnight.
But remember, everyone starts from zero followers and you truly never know what's going to resonate
with people.
I mean, I yell in my kitchen while I cook and people like it.
You never know if what you have to offer could really resonate with people.
So you might as well share it.
And once you've started building a following, use your broadcast channel.
That's how I like to let people know when I have big things coming.
Growing any size following is a big accomplishment.
And hitting 1 million followers is a huge milestone.
And there's more than one way to hit a million followers.
But what's worked for me is staying true to myself, sharing my real life and using the
tools available to me to grow closer to my audience every day.
And I'll see you next time.
I'll see you next time.

One of the coasters broke in half, and she ordered rock glue to put it back together.
It's just a coaster, so it's not a big deal.
It is so refreshing to hear it's not a big deal come out of an Airbnb host's mouth.
This host is awesome.
Biggest piece of damage was probably that the shelf was broken.
Mainly one of the kids used it as a ladder to climb onto the windowsill.
She said she tried to fix it, but obviously she didn't have a drill.
That was also a super quick fix.
Okay, that clip is like nine seconds, but it's very important.
Let's break down why.
One, she acknowledges kids are going to be kids.
They're going to break things.
It's no big deal.
Two, the guest should not be fixing this.
They don't have power tools.
It's not their responsibility.
And three, because she does have those tools, it's very easy for her to fix.
That, again, is just so refreshing to see.
Went to go cook the next day.
This burner wouldn't turn on at all.
You can see I was confused why it wasn't heating up.
I guess we're here for a whole month, so I'm not actually sure if it was their fault.
This is a really important skill for a host to have, which is understanding that there is
some damage that you can explicitly tie to a guest, to a reservation, and there is other
damage which you can't explicitly tie to them.
She acknowledges that right away in this clip, acknowledges that something's broken.
She doesn't know if they did it, and she's probably just going to have to fix it and
eat the cost.
I know I'm well known for a good hate watch, and I still am, but I really do like highlighting
hosts like these that are just awesome hosts that care about their guests, that aren't
petty, that aren't vindictive, and even when things go wrong, when things are broken, they
don't freak out about them.

corpus.caption:
I used @grok Bot to help my friend get a job after being laid off. 

I have a job hunting team of three Bots that work together for the sole purpose of securing a job for my friend. 

One Bot sorts through LinkedIn alerts arriving in his email account to select the best matches for my friend’s resume. Then, he will send the chosen postings to my recruiter Bot. 

My recruiter Bot will find relevant recruiters, their LinkedIn profiles and public email addresses to give my friend someone to contact at each company. This Bot will also draft an email or message my friend can send to the recruiters if he chooses to apply to the company. 

Lastly, my third Bot consolidates all this information on a website. This website, updated daily with new jobs to apply for, is sent to my friend’s email. The website contains the jobs, their posting dates, why he fits the role, the relevant recruiters and hiring managers, and any information the Bots could find regarding the interview loop as well. 

This has tremendously helped my friend’s job search, all thanks to Grok Bot by SpaceXAI. 

#grokbot #SpaceXAIPartner

transcript.text: My friend got laid off from his software engineering job,
and I'm using GrokBot by SpaceX AI to get him hired.
Meet my job hunting team.
I made a new email address, grabbed my friend's resume,
and connected it to my job hunting bot, Job.
Then I pointed LinkedIn, A16Z,
and every job board I could find at Job's inbox.
Job explains why each posting fits
and suggests resume tweaks for it.
He runs on his own cloud computer,
so he checks every three hours whether or not I'm around.
Job hands the new postings to Remy, my recruiter bot.
Remy tracks out who's hiring for each role,
digs up their contact details,
and drafts a note to send on LinkedIn or by email.
Then Remy and Job will send the postings,
reasoning, resume tweaks, and recruiter's information
to Newton in a channel that they all have together.
Newton turns all of it into a website
and emails my friend the link.
The website contains the jobs to apply to,
why he fits each one, his resume tweaks,
and the messages to the recruiters.
This has streamlined his process
and allowed him to meaningfully apply
to more jobs in less time.
Making my job hunting team was easy,
and if you want to build something similar,
you should go build your team of bots on GrokBot.

“Go get the money you’ve already earned.”

@rroomfies breaks down three tips for making real money on Facebook as a creator.

transcript.text: I made $261 my first month posting on Facebook
for doing literally nothing extra.
And guess what?
You don't need a huge following to start.
I only had 150 followers on Facebook
when I started cross-posting the reels
I was already posting on Instagram.
Facebook's monetization program pays out on qualified views,
so the content you're already making is what's making money.
Two things I wish I knew when I was just getting started.
Number one, don't just blindly post
because Facebook rewards original content.
Make sure the reels don't have any watermarkers.
And number two, give it 30 days before you judge.
My first week looked like nothing.
Facebook's audience views a little differently than Instagram,
so the posts that pop up aren't always the ones you'd expect.
You need to post in a volume to see a pattern.
To get started, just turn on professional mode
on your Facebook profile or use your page.
Number two, check your eligibility in your creator dashboard.
Number three, repost your existing content.
I started with reels, same captions I've used before and everything.
But you can also monetize text posts, photos, and stories on Facebook.
And number four, set up payments and let it run.
$261 isn't life-changing money.
Glad it's $261 for work I've already done.
If you're creating and Facebook isn't already in your strategy,
go get the money you've already earned.
Thank you.

transcript.text: This is the new Huawei Nova 16S Pro and it's the so-called king of AI selfies for 2026.
Even better, this guy finally supports 5G connectivity.
But how does it fare against the competition like the Galaxy S26 FE that we have here?
Let's see.
First up, the cameras.
The Nova 16S Pro clearly has an advantage here featuring true-to-color cameras on both the front and the rear.
Starting with selfies, Huawei is actually the first to introduce selfie zoom, so you can go as wide as 0.8x or up to 5x letting you capture stunning selfie portraits more easily.
This is where that King of AI selfies label really starts to make sense.
Because quality-wise, it's not even close.
Samsung's 12MP selfie camera, which doesn't even zoom, simply cannot keep up with Huawei's 50MP shooter.

Then around the back, Huawei has a 200-megapixel RYYB ultra-large sensor main camera, which can capture more light and detail, giving you higher quality photos and flexible cropping freedom versus Samsung's 50-megapixel main camera.
The same goes for both the ultra-wide and telephoto cameras, with Huawei boasting a 50-megapixel sensor as compared to Samsung's 12 and 8-megapixel cameras.
Which means no matter what you're trying to capture, you'd get more detailed shots and more true-to-life colors.
Battery life is yet another advantage for Huawei. It packs a large 7,000 mAh battery paired with a
faster 100W supercharge. Compare that to Samsung which only gets a 4900 mAh unit with a slower 45W
charging. Looking at our video loop test, the Galaxy S26 FE lasted about 29 hours. Although the
Nova 16S Pro takes it up a notch lasting nearly 52 hours. Lastly, there's the display and Huawei
one-ups the competition yet again with its larger 6.84-inch LTPO OLED screen. The panel is also
brighter, going up to 6,000 nits of peak brightness, and has a stronger Kunlun glass protection. This
means the Nova 16S Pro has a stronger drop and shatter resistance. On the other hand, the Galaxy
S26 FE sports a 6.7-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X screen, 1,900 nits of peak brightness, and Gorilla Glass
Victus Plus on top. All these advantages in the Nova 16S Pro still comes at a more affordable price.
For the 12 plus 256 gig config, the Nova 16S Pro will launch at only P399,999. Meanwhile,
the Galaxy S26 FE with the 8 plus 256 gig config is priced at P53,990. That said, initial impressions
for the Nova 16S Pro are looking pretty good. Also, the Huawei Nova 16S series has launched its
True Color Selfie Challenge on TikTok. If you're up to the task, submit your best selfie starting
from October 23 and get a chance to win one of 50 Nova 16S Pro units from over a 2 million peso
prize pool. That's it for now. Catch our full comparison soon on the YugoTek website and channels.

corpus.caption:
Fixing things shouldn’t be a radical act. It should be the standard. But most tech today is glued shut, making even a quick battery swap feel like rocket science.

At Fairphone, we do things differently. No glue. No secret tools. Just screws, modular parts, and tech designed to stay in your hands (and out of landfills) for as long as possible. Because when you can repair your device yourself, holding on to it for years becomes second nature.

So whether you're fixing an old appliance, helping a friend tune up their bike, or keeping your Fairphone going strong, happy International Repair Day! 🛠️

#Fairphone #TheOneThatLasts

transcript.text: I completely took apart the new Fairbuts 2 just to show you this. Putting them back together is
incredibly simple. Now, don't worry, you don't have to build these from scratch. I'm just doing
this to prove a point. Tech can be built to last. These earbuds feature Fairphone's signature modular
design. There are seven parts you can easily swap out using nothing but a screwdriver,
including replaceable batteries in both the earbuds and the charging case, all while still
being IP54 rated. Better yet, they're made with up to 46% fair and recycled materials,
they're 100% PFAS free, they support living wage bonuses and worker wellness programs,
and they come with warranty coverage up to three years. But building a more ethical earbud doesn't
mean compromising on sound. They're packing new 11mm biocellulose dynamic drivers, expertly tuned
by a professional acoustic engineering studio. And they're the first fairbuds to support LDAC
for near lossless high-res audio. They also feature improved transparency and active noise
cancellation modes. With multipoint Bluetooth, you can pair up to six devices and instantly
switch between two. All that with an impressive 40 hours of total battery life.

living in separate tabs.

Use my existing materials to put together

from the actual context of my business

which includes hiring help, something I have already done.
Six years in, I am finally building a business system.
that doesn't exclusively live in my head,

genes.label: Contrarian hook
genes.blurb: Opens with stop / never / don't / mistake / wrong.
genes.recipe: Open by calling out a mistake the viewer is making.

genes.label: Long caption
genes.blurb: Caption over 200 characters — tells a story.
genes.recipe: Write a long story caption (200+ chars).

genes.label: 30–60s
genes.blurb: Mid-form: 30 to 60 seconds.
genes.recipe: Give it room: 30 to 60 seconds.

genes.label: Fast pace (3+ w/s)
genes.blurb: Speaks at 3+ words per second.
genes.recipe: Cut every pause; script at ~3 words per second.

genes.label: Spoken CTA
genes.blurb: Asks to follow / comment / save / share.
genes.recipe: Close with one explicit ask: comment, save or follow.

genes.label: Original audio
genes.blurb: Uses the creator's own sound, not a track.
genes.recipe: Record your own audio instead of using a library track.

genes.label: 5+ hashtags

genes.recipe: Stack 5+ niche hashtags.

genes.label: Talks in < 0.5s
genes.blurb: First word lands within half a second.
genes.recipe: No intro, no breath — first word on frame one.

genes.label: 'I tried' experiment
genes.blurb: Personal test format: I tried / I tested / I spent.
genes.recipe: Frame it as a personal experiment with a result.

genes.label: Text-heavy
genes.blurb: Text overlay on most frames.
genes.recipe: Keep a text layer on screen almost the entire time.

genes.label: Screen recording
genes.blurb: Phone or computer screen capture.
genes.recipe: Show the screen — let them see it working.

genes.label: Text hook in first 3s
genes.blurb: On-screen text visible within the first 3 seconds.
genes.recipe: Burn a 3–6 word headline onto the opening frames.

genes.label: Text card
genes.blurb: Big text on a plain background.
genes.recipe: Open on a bold text card.

genes.label: 10–30s
genes.blurb: Classic short: 10 to 30 seconds.
genes.recipe: Land it between 10 and 30 seconds.

genes.label: Before / after
genes.blurb: Split or sequential before-and-after.
genes.recipe: Show the before, then the after.

genes.label: Direct 'you' hook
genes.blurb: First line addresses the viewer directly (you / your).
genes.recipe: Say 'you' in the first sentence — talk to one person, not an audience.

genes.label: Burned-in captions
genes.blurb: On-screen words mirror the spoken words.
genes.recipe: Add word-by-word captions that follow the voice.

genes.label: Short caption
genes.blurb: Caption under 60 characters.
genes.recipe: Keep the caption under 60 characters.

genes.label: No voice
genes.blurb: No speech — visuals, text and music carry it.
genes.recipe: Let visuals + on-screen text tell the story with zero voiceover.

genes.label: Hands + product
genes.blurb: Hands holding / demoing an object close-up.
genes.recipe: Show the thing in your hands, close to the lens.

genes.label: Licensed music
genes.blurb: Uses a copyrighted music track.
genes.recipe: Lay a recognisable licensed track under the video.

genes.label: 60s+
genes.blurb: Long-form short: over a minute.
genes.recipe: Go deep — over a minute is fine in this niche.

genes.label: POV / framing text
genes.blurb: Overlay frames the scene: POV / when / me when.
genes.recipe: Use a 'POV:' line to drop the viewer into the scene.

genes.label: Question hook
genes.blurb: First spoken line asks the viewer a question.
genes.recipe: Open by asking the exact question your viewer is already asking themselves.

genes.label: No hashtags
genes.blurb: Zero hashtags.
genes.recipe: Skip hashtags entirely.

genes.label: ALL-CAPS overlay
genes.blurb: Overlay set in capitals.
genes.recipe: Set the hook overlay in ALL CAPS.

brief.headline: Contrarian spoken hooks deliver an 18.96× lift—the single biggest lever in the dataset (n=3).
moves: Open with a contrarian spoken hook: it lifts views 18.96× (n=3, 9% of top quartile vs 0% of bottom).
Keep videos 30–60s (2.49× lift, n=41) and speak fast at 3+ words/sec (2.45× lift, n=38).
Use a long caption (3.03× lift, n=55) and add a spoken CTA (2.45× lift, n=8).
brief.avoid: Stop using ALL-CAPS overlays—they underperform at 0.27× lift (n=70).

I tried the most hyped AI tool for 30 days so you don't have to.
Most AI tools are useless—until you use them like this.
